solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Vehicle belonging to officer that stops working (7,6)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the noun: a strike that everyone joins, so work stops

blocks.note: a general is an officer; 'belonging to' makes it possessive, GENERAL'S
a trike is a three-wheeled vehicle

annotation.surface: An officer's car breaks down and won't go.
annotation.walkthrough: The break in the answer falls one letter away from the break in the wordplay: GENERAL'S TRIKE is re-spaced as GENERAL STRIKE.
annotation.definitionFit: A general strike is a stoppage of work across all trades at once.

entries.clue: Convey what one must do to reach the other side (3,6)

annotation.definition2: what one must do to reach the other side

blocks.note: to get an idea across is to convey it

blocks.clueFragment: what one must do to reach the other side

annotation.surface: Explaining how to get over a river or road.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is the literal phrase; the first is its figurative sense of making yourself understood.
annotation.definitionFit: To get a point across is to convey it successfully to a listener.

entries.clue: Well-known old man stops writer’s block? (7)

indicatorNotes.stops: the old man stops up the middle of the other word, like a plug in a hole

blocks.note: pa, a father, is the old man

annotation.surface: A famous old author is stuck and can't write.
annotation.walkthrough: Writer's block is normally an inability to write; the question mark allows it to be a literal block of paper for writing on.
annotation.definitionFit: A notepad is a block of paper sheets that a writer jots on.

entries.clue: Evocative piece for theremin is centrepiece (11)

indicatorNotes.piece for: the answer is a piece cut from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A reviewer praises an atmospheric composition for the theremin.
annotation.walkthrough: The theremin is the electronic instrument played without touching it; its name happens to end in REMIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Something reminiscent of the past evokes it, calling it to mind.

entries.clue: What breaks down fat in cheek when beginning to eat? (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: Something that burns fat in your face as you start eating.
annotation.walkthrough: Cheek is not the face here but sauciness, which is lip.
annotation.definitionFit: Lipase is the digestive enzyme that breaks down fats.

entries.clue: Bad faith mostly behind cast’s rage (5,1,3)

indicatorNotes.Bad: the letters are in a bad state, so they must be rearranged
indicatorNotes.mostly: most of the word, the last letter gone
indicatorNotes.behind: the anagram comes behind, after, the next piece

blocks.note: to cast is to throw; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: A theatre company's bad faith drives it to anger.
annotation.walkthrough: Cast reads as a group of actors; here it is the verb throw.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase names a sudden tantrum, so the verb phrase stands for the verb rage.

entries.clue: Boring relic I smashed is beyond repair (12)

indicatorNotes.smashed: the words are smashed to pieces and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A dull old relic, broken by me, can't be fixed.
annotation.walkthrough: Incorrigible usually describes people, but its root sense is 'cannot be corrected', which is fair for beyond repair.
annotation.definitionFit: Something incorrigible cannot be corrected or reformed, so it is beyond repair.

entries.clue: This fanatic could make us hesitant (10)

indicatorNotes.could make: the letters could be made into the answer by rearranging

annotation.surface: Someone so zealous that the rest of us hold back.
annotation.walkthrough: The joke is the opposite fit: a keen enthusiast makes everyone else cautious.
annotation.definitionFit: An enthusiast is a fervent devotee, a fan or fanatic.

entries.clue: Release payment (9)

blocks.note: the release of a patient from hospital or a soldier from service
payment that settles a debt in full, in formal legal language

annotation.surface: Money handed over at the moment of release.
annotation.walkthrough: Both senses are nouns here: a discharge from hospital, and the discharge of a debt.
annotation.definitionFit: A discharge is a release, and discharging a debt means paying it.

entries.clue: Demerger of company possibly finishing early in March? (4)

indicatorNotes.finishing early: the word finishes one letter early, losing its last letter

blocks.note: demob, demobilisation, breaks up a military company

annotation.surface: A firm's split is due to complete ahead of schedule in March.
annotation.walkthrough: Demerger is business jargon, but the company is a military unit being stood down; March is a protest, not the month.
annotation.definitionFit: A demo, a demonstration, is often a protest march; the question mark flags the example.

entries.clue: Croatian celebrity’s mercurial character (5,11)

blocks.note: Split is a Croatian port city
a personality is a celebrity; the 's is 'is'

annotation.surface: A Croatian star is known for being moody.
annotation.walkthrough: Croatian reads as a nationality; it stands for a place in Croatia.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone with a split personality switches unpredictably between moods, as a mercurial person does.

entries.clue: Cruel king died at the foot of illustrious man (5)

indicatorNotes.at the foot of: in a down clue, the foot is the bottom, so the letter goes after

blocks.note: a hero is an illustrious man
D is the standard abbreviation for died

annotation.surface: A tyrant dies at the feet of a great man.
annotation.walkthrough: Herod the Great ordered the Massacre of the Innocents in the Gospel story.
annotation.definitionFit: Herod is the biblical king known for his cruelty.

entries.clue: Imperial family’s month south of Italian capital (7)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, south is below, so the month follows

blocks.note: NOV is the abbreviation for November

annotation.surface: A royal family takes a month's holiday south of Rome.
annotation.walkthrough: Italian capital means the Italian name for the capital, not its first letter I.
annotation.definitionFit: The Romanovs were the imperial dynasty of Russia until 1917.

entries.clue: Part of camera appearance on television perhaps satisfied former monarch (8,5)

blocks.note: met = satisfied, as in met the demand
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was the Queen

annotation.surface: A camera shows a TV appearance that pleased an ex-king.
annotation.walkthrough: ER is former now that Elizabeth II has died.
annotation.definitionFit: An exposure meter measures light to set a camera's exposure, and may be built in.

entries.clue: Bear marks object of symbolic significance (5)

blocks.note: to tote is to carry, bear
M is the abbreviation for the mark, the old German currency

annotation.surface: A bear leaves claw marks on a sacred emblem.
annotation.walkthrough: Bear is the verb carry, not the animal, and marks are the currency.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is an object revered as a symbol of a clan or group.

entries.clue: Laptop camera losing power damaged tablet? (11)

indicatorNotes.losing: the phrase loses the letter that follows
indicatorNotes.damaged: the remaining letters are damaged, rearranged

blocks.note: P = power; one P of LAPTOP goes

annotation.surface: A laptop's webcam stops working, and so does the tablet computer.
annotation.walkthrough: Tablet seems to continue the computing theme; it is a pill.
annotation.definitionFit: Paracetamol is a painkiller commonly taken as a tablet; the question mark marks it as one example.

entries.clue: Reassign motorway area covered by salesman (5)

indicatorNotes.covered by: the motorway and area are covered, enclosed, by the salesman

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1
A is the standard abbreviation for area

annotation.surface: A sales rep's territory covering the motorway is redrawn.
annotation.walkthrough: British motorways are numbered with M, as in the M25 round London.
annotation.definitionFit: To remap keys or functions is to assign them afresh.

entries.clue: Maxim presumably helping to manage cutting-edge technology (6,3)

blocks.note: coping is managing; the saw, presumably, helps you cope
a saw is an old saying, a maxim

annotation.surface: A proverb supposedly helps you handle the latest tech.
annotation.walkthrough: Cutting-edge means advanced; taken literally, a saw's technology is its cutting edge.
annotation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a fine-bladed hand saw, literally a tool with a cutting edge.

entries.clue: Swapping sides in period of military service results in heavy defeat (4)

indicatorNotes.Swapping sides: the sides of a word are its first and last letters, and they change places

annotation.surface: Soldiers changing sides mid-tour end up badly beaten.
annotation.walkthrough: Swapping sides suggests defection; here the two end letters trade places.
annotation.definitionFit: A rout is a crushing defeat with the losers put to flight.

entries.clue: Trainees dispatched, having succeeded finally with previous boss (8)

indicatorNotes.finally: the S for succeeded moves to the final position
indicatorNotes.previous: the boss comes previous to, before, the rest

blocks.note: a boss is a round knob or stud
SENT = dispatched, with its S (succeeded, as in family trees) moved to the end

annotation.surface: Trainees are sent off once they have done well under their former manager.
annotation.walkthrough: Boss is not a manager but a raised ornament, a stud.
annotation.definitionFit: Students are learners, people in training.

entries.clue: Flowers merry widow laid regularly (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: take letters at a regular interval, every second one

annotation.surface: Flowers are laid on a grave by a cheerful widow.
annotation.walkthrough: The Merry Widow is an operetta, which helps hide merry as a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Gladioli are tall flowering plants with sword-shaped leaves.

entries.clue: Rather strange hairstyle repulsed attractive person (6)

indicatorNotes.repulsed: pushed back, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a do, a hairdo, read backwards
a dish is a good-looking person

annotation.surface: A weird haircut puts off a handsome date.
annotation.walkthrough: Repulsed means disgusted in the surface; in the wordplay it means pushed back.
annotation.definitionFit: The -ish ending softens odd to somewhat odd, rather strange.

entries.clue: Estate manager recognised flower outside English church (8,8)

indicatorNotes.outside: the flower goes outside, around, the next letters

blocks.note: a flower is something that flows, a river

annotation.surface: A gardener recognised a bloom beside an English church.
annotation.walkthrough: Flower is the crossword's river, a thing that flows; an official receiver runs a bankrupt's estate.
annotation.definitionFit: An official receiver is appointed to manage the estate of a bankrupt.

entries.clue: Remove level after end of game (5)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter
indicatorNotes.after: the level word comes after that letter

blocks.note: rase is a variant spelling of raze, to level

annotation.surface: Wipe the level once the game ends.
annotation.walkthrough: Level is a verb, to raze, here in the older spelling rase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, narrowed: erasing removes marks or data by wiping them out.

entries.clue: Court directive’s support reportedly governing organisation (11,5)

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported, spoken: the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: a rest supports, like an armrest
an order is an organisation, such as a monastic order

annotation.surface: A court's ruling is said to support the governing body.
annotation.walkthrough: Reportedly applies only to governing; the other pieces are spelt as they are.
annotation.definitionFit: A restraining order is a court injunction keeping one person away from another.

entries.clue: Bold expression of gallery pieces in stone (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the gallery and pieces go in the stone

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
the Tate is the London art gallery

annotation.surface: A gallery's stone sculpture makes a daring impression.
annotation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A statement, as in a fashion statement, is a bold way of expressing something.

entries.clue: Brings together group involved in team assessments (7)

indicatorNotes.involved in: the answer is involved, contained, in the next words

blocks.note: a group is a mass, the core of the answer

annotation.surface: Managers gather everyone for team appraisals.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is hidden whole; 'group' only points to the MASS in its middle.
annotation.definitionFit: To amass things is to bring them together in quantity.

entries.clue: Home team start to show guts (7)

indicatorNotes.start to: the start of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: The home side begins to show courage.
annotation.walkthrough: Guts reads as courage; it is the literal innards.
annotation.definitionFit: Your insides are your guts, the internal organs.

entries.clue: Record almost everything of dreadful quality (5)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost all of the word: its last letter goes

annotation.surface: Nearly every track on a record is awful.
annotation.walkthrough: Bum as an adjective, as in a bum deal, means of poor quality.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from music: a long-playing collection of tracks is released as a record.

entries.clue: Scrapped qualification overwhelming unprepared learner (7)

indicatorNotes.overwhelming: the qualification overwhelms, swallows, the next letters

blocks.note: BEd, Bachelor of Education, a teaching degree
L for learner, as on a British L-plate

annotation.surface: A course was cancelled because students came unprepared.
annotation.walkthrough: Scrapped looks like cancelled; it is the past tense of scrap, to fight.
annotation.definitionFit: To scrap is to fight, so those who scrapped brawled.

entries.clue: Congress would not be able to pass such a measure (8,4)

annotation.definition: Congress would not be able to pass such a measure

blocks.note: reads as the US legislature; the setter means its old sense of sexual intercourse

blocks.clueFragment: would not be able to pass such a measure
blocks.note: reads as a bill failing; the measure is a locked garment that nothing gets past

annotation.surface: A bill so contentious the US legislature could never pass it.
annotation.walkthrough: Congress looks like the American parliament and measure like a bill; congress also means sex, and the measure is a physical barrier to it.
annotation.definitionFit: A chastity belt was a locked garment to prevent sexual intercourse.

entries.clue: Vehicle regulator announced staff’s important role in experiment (6,7)

indicatorNotes.announced: spoken aloud, so the word is heard, not spelt

blocks.note: the control group is the untreated baseline an experiment is compared against

annotation.surface: A car's speed limiter is declared essential to the staff's test.
annotation.walkthrough: Announced sounds only the crew's; control is spelt as is.
annotation.definitionFit: Cruise control keeps a car at a set speed, regulating the vehicle.

entries.clue: Shot part of news report (8)

blocks.note: to be in something is to be part of it

annotation.surface: Footage of a gunshot appears in the news.
annotation.walkthrough: Part of gives IN, as in 'in the team'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from broadcasting: the short scheduled news update on radio or television.

entries.clue: Compensate district court with time rather than money ultimately (10)

indicatorNotes.rather than: the time replaces the money letter
indicatorNotes.ultimately: the ultimate, last, letter of money

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
last letter of money, which ERA replaces
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A county court awards time served instead of damages.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a judgement awarding a prison term instead of a fine; 'rather than' is a swap instruction, one piece standing in for another.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: acting against an effect offsets it, making up for it.

entries.clue: Look convinced about president’s compulsion to emulate others (4,8)

indicatorNotes.about: the president's letters go about, around, the next word

annotation.surface: Staring, sure of the president's urge to copy everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s supplies a letter of its own here, so president's is P plus S.
annotation.definitionFit: Peer pressure is the social push to act like the people around you.

entries.clue: Board of international organisation keeping united front for Israel is inappropriate (10)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the board keeps the letters inside it
indicatorNotes.front: the front of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: UN, the United Nations, with the 's of 'of international organisation'
I is the abbreviation for Israel

annotation.surface: A UN board's support for Israel is judged improper.
annotation.walkthrough: Board of international organisation is the UN's table, UNSTABLE, which then keeps U and I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something not fitting the occasion is out of place.

entries.clue: Partially erected folly disturbed charming scene (5)

indicatorNotes.Partially: only part of the following words is used
indicatorNotes.erected: in a down clue, erected means set upright, read from bottom to top

annotation.surface: A half-built garden folly has been vandalised in a lovely setting.
annotation.walkthrough: A folly is an ornamental building in a park; erected looks like building, but it means turning the letters upright.
annotation.definitionFit: An idyll is an idealised, picturesque scene of peace.

entries.clue: One who wastes more than most (6,6)

annotation.definition: One who wastes more than most

blocks.note: reads as a spendthrift; waste is gangster slang for murder
reads as extravagance; the setter means many victims, one after another

annotation.surface: A spendthrift who squanders more than anyone.
annotation.walkthrough: Wastes looks like squanders; in gangster slang, to waste someone is to murder them.
annotation.definitionFit: A serial killer murders many people, more than most killers.

entries.clue: Special ban destroyed last of industry inevitably (11)

indicatorNotes.destroyed: the letters are destroyed and rebuilt
indicatorNotes.last of: take the last letter of the word

annotation.surface: A special ban has wrecked what remained of industry, as was bound to happen.
annotation.walkthrough: The Y joins the anagram fodder before the letters are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Inescapably means in a way that cannot be avoided, inevitably.

entries.clue: Intimate books yielding pleasant embraces (4,6)

indicatorNotes.embraces: the pleasant word embraces, wraps round, the books

blocks.note: to give is to yield, as a floor gives underfoot

annotation.surface: Racy books offer pleasant cuddles.
annotation.walkthrough: Intimate looks like an adjective, close; it is the verb meaning to announce formally.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal sense: intimate as a verb means to announce or notify officially.

entries.clue: Fresh troops evacuated subway (5)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: emptied of its insides, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the SAS, the British Army's Special Air Service

annotation.surface: New troops clear an underground passage.
annotation.walkthrough: Fresh means cheeky here, not new.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone fresh is impertinent, cheeky, sassy.

entries.clue: Sick reindeer with docked tail requiring more attention (7)

indicatorNotes.with docked tail: the word's tail, its last letter, is cut off

annotation.surface: An ill reindeer with a clipped tail needs extra care.
annotation.walkthrough: Docked is the word for cutting an animal's tail, which suits the reindeer.
annotation.definitionFit: A comparative for a comparative: a child in more need calls for more care.

entries.clue: Imbecile destined to possess brains (9)

indicatorNotes.to possess: the destined word possesses, holds, the brains

annotation.surface: A fool is fated to be clever.
annotation.walkthrough: Imbecile is an adjective here, meaning stupid.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial synonym: a fathead is a dolt, and the adjective means foolish.

entries.clue: Striking skill involved with boring pastime (9)

indicatorNotes.boring: IN bores into, is placed inside, the pastime

blocks.note: to be in with is to be involved with

annotation.surface: A dull hobby calls for a remarkable talent.
annotation.walkthrough: Striking looks like impressive; a striker's skill in football is finishing, putting chances away.
annotation.definitionFit: Finishing is a striker's skill of converting chances into goals.

entries.clue: What evildoer owes according to Reverend Spooner’s service (6,3)

indicatorNotes.according to Reverend Spooner’s: Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: what one owes is a debt

annotation.surface: What a wrongdoer is owed at a church service, says the Reverend.
annotation.walkthrough: Sinner's debt with the S and D swapped gives dinner set.
annotation.definitionFit: A dinner service is a full set of plates and dishes, a dinner set.

entries.clue: Tolerably polite act of manipulation that helps to build bridges (5,11)

annotation.definitionNote: a relative clause standing for the noun

blocks.note: engineering a result is manipulating it

annotation.surface: Grudging courtesy and scheming as ways to heal a rift.
annotation.walkthrough: Build bridges suggests making peace; here the bridges are real.
annotation.definitionFit: Civil engineering is the discipline that designs and builds bridges, roads and the like.

entries.clue: Brought up small child borne by very old daughter (7)

indicatorNotes.borne by: the child is carried inside the other letters

blocks.note: a mite is a small child

annotation.surface: A child was raised by a very old mother.
annotation.walkthrough: Brought up looks like raised; it means threw up.
annotation.definitionFit: To bring up food is to vomit it.

entries.clue: This may be viewed on the outside of computer’s case (6)

annotation.definition: This may be viewed on the outside of computer’s case

indicatorNotes.on the outside of: the viewed word goes on the outside, around, what follows
indicatorNotes.case: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters

blocks.note: CompuR... outer letters: C and R

annotation.surface: A description of a monitor fixed to the outside of a PC.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a screen is what you view on the computer's case.
annotation.definitionFit: The &lit reads straight: the monitor sits on the front of the machine, the part you look at.

entries.clue: Rare event of horse scratching bottom on cow (7)

indicatorNotes.scratching bottom: the bottom, last, letter is scratched out
indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the cow

blocks.note: an ox is a bovine; loosely, cow

annotation.surface: An unusual sight of a horse scratching its rear on a cow.
annotation.walkthrough: Rare is fair: an equinox happens only twice a year.
annotation.definitionFit: An equinox, when day and night are equal, occurs just twice a year.

entries.clue: Suddenly attack exciting idea? (4-2)

annotation.definitionNote: the answer is TURN ON as a verb for the first sense and TURN-ON as a noun for the second

blocks.note: a phrasal verb for rounding on someone without warning
a noun for anything that arouses interest or desire

annotation.surface: A thrilling notion strikes out of nowhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The hyphen suits the noun; the question mark says the idea is only one kind of turn-on.
annotation.definitionFit: Turn on means to attack suddenly, and a turn-on is something arousing or exciting.

entries.clue: Pardon me! It’s wrong to mention somebody you know (4-4)

annotation.definition: It’s wrong to mention somebody you know

blocks.note: reads as an apology; it is the false modesty that comes with the boast

blocks.clueFragment: It’s wrong to mention somebody you know
blocks.note: reads as a rule of discretion; the setter means casually citing famous acquaintances

annotation.surface: An apology for mentioning a famous friend.
annotation.walkthrough: Pardon me! is the name-dropper's fake modesty, as in 'Pardon me, but when I met the Queen...'
annotation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous people you know, which is frowned on.

entries.clue: Angry with fivefold increase initially in rubbish (5)

indicatorNotes.with fivefold increase initially: the first letter, C for 100, grows five times to D for 500

annotation.surface: Furious about a huge rise in waste.
annotation.walkthrough: The increase is in Roman numerals: C is 100 and D is 500.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: literally the scum skimmed off molten metal, hence any worthless stuff.

entries.clue: Upmarket magazine uncovered what’s missing (4)

indicatorNotes.uncovered: the cover, the first and last letters, is taken off

blocks.note: a glossy is a high-end magazine

annotation.surface: A posh magazine exposes a hidden gap.
annotation.walkthrough: Uncovered suggests an exposé; it strips the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the thing that has been lost, the shortfall after the fact.

entries.clue: Artwork certainly encapsulates pressure inherent in religious belief (9)

indicatorNotes.encapsulates: the certainly word encapsulates, encloses, what follows
indicatorNotes.inherent in: the pressure sits inside the religious belief

blocks.note: a cult is a religious movement

annotation.surface: A work of art is sure to capture the strains of faith.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: 'inherent in' works inside the phrase that 'encapsulates' then wraps.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: carved or modelled three-dimensional pieces are one kind of artwork.

entries.clue: Notice faculty that’s disputed closure of university (4)

indicatorNotes.closure of: the close of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is a contested faculty

annotation.surface: A department under dispute is told the university will close.
annotation.walkthrough: Faculty looks like a university department; it is a mental power.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary synonym: to catch sight of something in the distance.

entries.clue: Helping mainly to get a sense of proportion (5)

indicatorNotes.mainly: the main part of the word, losing its last letter

blocks.note: a helping is a fixed portion or allowance, especially of food

annotation.surface: Portion control helps you keep things in proportion.
annotation.walkthrough: Helping reads as assisting; it is a portion of food.
annotation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses one quantity in proportion to another.

entries.clue: Desperate state of French government’s rules repulsing Conservative (11)

indicatorNotes.repulsing: the rules repulse, push out, the Conservative

blocks.note: a constitution sets out a government's rules

annotation.surface: France's government is in a dire state after rejecting the right.
annotation.walkthrough: CON is the standard short form of Conservative, the British right-wing party.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, narrowed: the desperate state is utter poverty, lacking even necessities.

entries.clue: Refusal to stop membership fee brought about unexpected reward (5)

indicatorNotes.to stop: the refusal stops up, plugs, the middle of the fee
indicatorNotes.brought about: turned about, so the whole reads backwards

annotation.surface: Refusing to pay a club's fee brought an unexpected windfall.
annotation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the turnaround second, so the reversal applies to the whole assembly, not just the fee.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an extra payment on top of what was due, often a windfall.

entries.clue: Perverted server of queen seduced by Zeus? (3,6)

blocks.note: Leda, queen of Sparta, seduced by Zeus as a swan, with 's
a tray serves food and drink

annotation.surface: A corrupted waiter to the Spartan queen Zeus seduced.
annotation.walkthrough: In myth Zeus came to Leda, queen of Sparta, in the form of a swan; 'server of queen' is the queen's server, with the word break moved.
annotation.definitionFit: To be led astray is to be corrupted, perverted from the right path.

entries.clue: Departure gate for vital flight? (9,4)

blocks.note: reads as an airport gate; the setter means any way out
reads as an important plane; the flight is fleeing from danger

annotation.surface: An airport gate for an important plane.
annotation.walkthrough: Departure gate and flight say airport; the flight is an escape, the gate a door out in a crisis.
annotation.definitionFit: An emergency exit is the door used for urgent flight from danger.
